The kernel is complete at [output_model_new.py](/root/lumen-clean/lumen-sosp26-ae-origin/runs/kernelbench_generation_level1_moonbridge/p22/round0/output_model_new.py).

**Results:** compiled ✓, correctness 5/5 ✓, runtime 2.93ms vs 2.30ms reference (~27% slower).

The implementation uses a single `@avelang.jit` kernel with `al.Pointer` + `al.make_tensor` for the 1.6B-element runtime-shaped tensor (static `al.Tensor` would blow up MLIR codegen at this scale). The kernel converts each bf16 element to f32, computes `al.tanh` (lowers to `__ocml_tanh_f32` on AMD), converts back to bf16, and writes the result. A grid-stride loop with 256 threads × 131072 blocks covers all elements with each thread processing ~48 elements.

Things I tried that didn't work out:
- **BF16-direct tanh**: linker fails with "no libcall available for ftanh" — `al.tanh` only has an f32 lowering
- **Hardware exp-based tanh**: formula `2/(1+e^(-2x))-1` using `al.exp` (hardware-accelerated `llvm.amdgcn.exp`) was actually slower (3.09ms) than the software tanh library call
- **Vectorized loads**: `raw_buffer_load_x4` + `al.view` approach compiled but produced incorrect results (0.238 max diff), likely a view mutation/writeback issue
- **Block sizes > 256**: all failed with HIP launch errors, suggesting register pressure or workgroup size constraints on this hardware
